name: Rytr
subcategory: AI drafting, research and content optimization
tagline: Generate short-form copy from structured templates and reusable tone settings

tiers.name: Unlimited
tiers.limits: Unlimited generations; 1 tone match; 50 plagiarism checks/month; 1 language; 2× input allowance.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Unlimited generations; multiple tone matches; 100 plagiarism checks/month; 35+ languages; 3× input allowance.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 10,000 characters/month; 1 language; 20+ tones; no plagiarism checks
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual advertised as 2 months free)

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Rytr, generate short-form copy from structured templates and reusable tone settings. The hard boundary is template breadth, hosted model access, and browser extension convenience, plus workflow, data, and model tuning.
coreLoopDIY: Take a brief, generate short-form copy from structured templates and reusable tone settings, and keep citations and revisions attached to each section.
whatYouLose: template breadth, hosted model access, and browser extension convenience
ongoingBurden: prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Rytr because the subscription bundles a refined workflow, proprietary signals, templates, and predictable output quality for a team. The recurring cost buys prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Open WebUI
priorArt.desc: Active open-source interface for local and API-backed language models with retrieval features.

alternatives.name: AnythingLLM
alternatives.desc: A local-first AI desk with reusable agents, documents, memory, and workflows; less campaign theatre, more settings.

facts.install: Desktop installer for macOS/Windows/Linux, or Docker for a self-hosted web instance
facts.engines: Local llama.cpp models plus Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI and many cloud APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter and Mistral
facts.dataFormat: Desktop data stays in the app's local storage; self-hosted data is stored in the mounted server storage and chosen vector database (LanceDB by default), while prompts sent to cloud models leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It can save tone instructions and prompts, but Rytr's immediate structured templates and low-friction hosted writing flow are less work for a non-expert.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is easy, but useful results still require downloading a local model or supplying a model-provider API key

alternatives.name: Jan
alternatives.desc: A desktop local-model writer with reusable assistants and projects; templates are prompts you save yourself.

facts.install: Download the macOS, Windows or Linux desktop installer
facts.engines: Built-in local inference via llama.cpp/llama-server plus OpenAI-compatible APIs and connectors such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter
facts.dataFormat: Threads, assistants, settings and downloaded model files live in Jan's local data folder; only requests sent to configured cloud providers leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: You must build each use case as a prompt or assistant, losing Rytr's ready-made templates, tone picker, and one-click simplicity.
facts.setupBlocker: Local use requires downloading a multi-gigabyte model and enough RAM; cloud use requires an API key

alternatives.name: Witsy
alternatives.desc: System-wide selected-text commands, reusable experts, a scratchpad, and document context; bring the model and skip the subscription.

facts.install: Download a desktop binary from GitHub Releases; macOS also supports `brew install --cask witsy`
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, xAI, Meta, Ollama, LM Studio, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Groq, Cerebras, Azure and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, plus optional image, video, speech, search and MCP providers
facts.dataFormat: Conversation history, experts, settings and document repositories live in the local application profile; local files are indexed locally, while prompts and retrieved context sent to a cloud model leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: Its reusable experts are flexible, but they require more configuration than Rytr's guided templates and built-in tone controls.
facts.setupBlocker: It is BYOK unless you install Ollama and a local model; system-wide commands also need OS accessibility permissions

alternatives.name: Writing Tools
alternatives.desc: Select text anywhere, hit a hotkey, and fix, rewrite, summarize, or obey a custom instruction without opening another tab.

facts.install: Use the portable Windows ZIP or macOS DMG; Linux currently runs from source
facts.engines: Gemini, native Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible cloud or local endpoint on Windows/Linux; the macOS port also supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, OpenRouter, Gemini, MLX and Ollama
facts.dataFormat: API keys and configuration stay on the device; the app does not retain writing or logs, and selected text goes only to the chosen cloud provider unless a local model is used
facts.gapVsPaid: It excels at rewriting selected text, not Rytr's blank-page generation flow with a catalog of marketing use cases and reusable tones.
facts.setupBlocker: You must supply an API key or install a local model; macOS needs Accessibility permissions, while Linux installation and Wayland support remain rough

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Unlimited plan and a personal content workstation DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Rytr in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and the OpenAI Responses API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: take a brief, generate short-form copy from structured templates and reusable tone settings, and keep citations and revisions attached to each section.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Build a brief form with audience, objective, tone, source URLs, and prohibited claims.
Store imported source text locally and chunk it for retrieval with SQLite FTS5.
Generate an outline first and require approval before drafting sections.
Attach source references to generated paragraphs and flag unsupported claims.
Provide rewrite controls for shorten, clarify, change tone, and add evidence.
Export clean Markdown plus a JSON research bundle.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out live search-engine rank data.
Deliberately leave out automatic publishing to third-party CMSs.
Deliberately leave out multi-user approvals and brand governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
